title: Private: add per-cluster backup success objective + error budget reporting
author: Rafael Mendes
release_notes:
- Adds internal SLO-like objective for Private backup success (per cluster) with error-budget style reporting for SRE and oncall.
- Introduces recommended alerting for missed backup windows and fast/slow burn of backup failure budget.
body:
Context
SRE needs a consistent, per-cluster objective for scheduled backup reliability in Redwood Private deployments (VPC + on-prem). This PR adds an internal SLO-like objective for “backup jobs succeed” and wires it into error-budget reporting that we can use during DR readiness reviews and incident response.

Scope
- Defines a per-cluster objective measuring scheduled backup job success over a 28d window.
- Adds error-budget reporting (remaining budget + burn rate) that can be used for quarterly DR game day readiness and for noisy-cluster triage.
- Adds alert rules tuned for two classes of failure:
  (1) missed backup window / no successful backup in N hours
  (2) rapid burn (many failures) indicating systemic issues (permissions, storage throttling, DB contention)

Metric contract (assumptions)
This assumes observability-pack emits counters with these labels (already in-flight / landed in other repos):
- redwood_private_backup_jobs_total{cluster_id, backup_type="scheduled", result="success"|"failure", reason?}
- redwood_private_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds{cluster_id}
If your environment uses different label keys (e.g., cluster instead of cluster_id), see README note below.

Objective definition
- Service: private-backup (logical service; grouped by cluster_id)
- SLI: success ratio = sum(rate(success)) / sum(rate(total))
- Window: 28d
- Target: 99.0% success (scheduled backups)
Rationale: we want “some failures tolerated” (storage transient errors, operator maintenance) but a clear error-budget signal when reliability degrades. We can tune to 99.5% after a couple quarters of data.

Alerting
Adds multi-window, multi-burn alerting (fast + slow) plus a simpler symptom alert.
- Fast burn: 2h/30m windows (paging) when burn rate threatens budget quickly.
- Slow burn: 6h/1d windows (ticket) to catch creeping issues.
- Symptom: “last successful scheduled backup age” (warn) with pause/disable suppression support.

Suppression / paused clusters
We support a common ops pattern where a cluster’s scheduled backups are intentionally paused (e.g., during a restore drill or migration). This PR includes a recommended convention:
- redwood_private_backup_slo_enabled{cluster_id} = 0/1 (recording rule or static series via kube-state-metrics / prom operator)
Alert rules and SLO calculation can be gated on enabled==1.

Changes
- slos/private/private-backup-success.yaml: new objective + alerting rules
- lib/sli/backup_success_ratio.libsonnet: helper for computing success ratio and gating on enabled
- dashboards/error_budget/private_backup.jsonnet: error budget burn + remaining budget panels
- docs/private-backup-slo.md: metric contract + rollout guidance
- tests/slo_private_backup_success_test.yaml: golden tests for rule rendering
- CHANGELOG.md: entry for v0.14.0

Example (snippet)
Objective (rendered):
- name: private-backup-success
  target: 0.99
  sli:
    events:
      errorQuery: sum by (cluster_id) (rate(redwood_private_backup_jobs_total{result="failure",backup_type="scheduled"}[{{.window}}]))
      totalQuery: sum by (cluster_id) (rate(redwood_private_backup_jobs_total{backup_type="scheduled"}[{{.window}}]))
  alerting:
    pageAlert:
      burnrates: [14.4, 6]
      windows: ["30m", "2h"]

Rollout plan
- Land in slo-toolkit and start generating rules for internal SRE prometheus.
- Enable for pilot Private clusters first (design partners), then expand.
- After 2-4 weeks, evaluate whether target/alerts need adjustment (especially on-prem environments with restricted storage endpoints).

Notes for oncall
- Error budget is meant as a reliability signal, not a compliance mechanism.
- When budget burn is observed, refer to the backup failure troubleshooting runbook (Confluence) and validate: storage IAM/KMS perms, backup job concurrency, DB lock contention.

Related
- Linear: ENG-4869 (Observability requirements—metrics, dashboards, and alerts for backup/restore)
- Project epic: ENG-4821 (Day-2 Ops Toolkit: Backup/Restore (Private))

review_conversation:
Sean Gallagher (review): Target=99% feels low; do we have any data to support? Also, please ensure we don’t page for clusters that have backups intentionally disabled during maintenance.
Rafael Mendes (author): Agreed on target; set to 99.0% as starting point with intent to ratchet after a quarter. Added gating support via redwood_private_backup_slo_enabled{cluster_id} and documented the convention in docs/private-backup-slo.md.

Allison Grant (review): Metric naming: we should avoid coupling to reason labels that might not exist everywhere. Also dashboard should show last success age alongside burn.
Rafael Mendes (author): Removed reason label usage from queries; kept it optional for drill-down only. Added last_success panels to the dashboard jsonnet.

Sergio Costa (review): Can we add a slow-burn ticket alert rather than paging only? And label the alerts with the runbook URL convention.
Rafael Mendes (author): Added slow-burn alert and runbook_url annotation. Runbook link matches the alert annotation convention used by observability-pack.

Miles Thornton (review): The burn rate thresholds look aggressive for low-frequency jobs. If backups are hourly, a couple failures can look like rapid burn.
Rafael Mendes (author): Good call—switched the fast-burn to require at least min_total_events over the short window by using the totalQuery guard and documented the assumption that backup frequency >= hourly. We can revise once we have more on-prem cadence data.

Sean Gallagher (final): LGTM with gating + docs changes.
